title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): Grothendieck studies spaces Σ^A(n) attached to a stratified space. These are 'unfolding' (déploiement) spaces indexed by finite totally ordered sets. He restricts to strictly increasing maps d ↪ d' with d cofinal in d'. This category is equivalent to that of (possibly empty) totally ordered sets d, via d ↦ d ⊔ {ω} with ω a last element. So one gets a functor Γ : d ↦ Σ^A(d ⊔ {ω}) on finite ordinals with injective monotone maps. Such a Γ is the same thing as an augmented semi-simplicial object: Γ(∅) together with a semi-simplicial space over it.

This page:
1. The base is Γ(∅) = Σ (written Σ^*(0) or Σ^*(ω)). The rest of Γ is a semi-simplicial space relative to Σ.
2. Earlier conditions b1, b2, b3 constrain this relative structure. They say it comes from a 'locally cylindrical' stratification of Σ. The model is normal-crossing or corner type: near each point, a stratum of codimension k is locally the intersection of k codimension-one local branches.
3. The stratification is moreover 'ordered'. At each x ∈ Σ, the germs of codimension-1 strata through x are totally ordered, and this order varies continuously with x.
4. Under these conditions, Γ(d) = Σ^*(d+1) (margin NB: Γ(n) = Σ^*(n+1)) is the space of germs of strata of codimension d+1. Here d is read as an ordinal with d+1 elements. Equivalently, it is the space of increasing (d+1)-tuples of distinct codimension-1 germs at a point.
5. The face maps (deleting an element of the tuple) come from the order structure.
6. The purpose is to reconstruct the unfolding spaces of the stratification from the Γ(d), using the order.
7. Conversely, giving Γ with its semi-simplicial operators is claimed equivalent to giving Σ with an ordered locally cylindrical stratification.

The next page makes this precise:
- Γ_0 is the étalé-type space of codimension-1 germs over Σ.
- Γ'(d) is the relative d-fold fibre power of Γ_0 over Σ, minus the images of the partial diagonals; on that page d counts the elements of the tuple.
- Γ'(d) ≅ 𝔖_d × Γ(d).
- A relative total order is a clopen Γ_1 ⊂ Γ_0 ×_Σ Γ_0 \ diag such that Γ_1 and its transpose partition that set, with a transitivity condition.

In modern terms, this is the semi-simplicial space of 'normalized' strata of a normal-crossings / corner-type stratification. Examples are Deligne's D^{[k]} for a simple normal crossings divisor, and the k-fold boundary of a manifold with corners. The novelty is that the ordering of local branches is only a continuously varying local order, not a global numbering of components.
errors: Index conventions are loose. On this page Γ(d) = Σ^*(d+1) treats d as an ordinal with d+1 elements, while the next page uses d for the number of elements in the fibre power. This is harmless but inconsistent.

The claimed equivalence between Γ and an ordered locally cylindrical stratification of Σ is only asserted. It also needs the conditions b1–b3 (not visible here) to force each codim-(d+1) germ to be determined by a set of d+1 distinct codim-1 germs. This is a corner/normal-crossing hypothesis; it fails for general conical singularities.

The 'germs of strata' must be understood as local branches, not global strata; for self-intersecting strata the distinction matters. The text gestures at this with '(germes de)' but does not make it precise.

ideas.what: Encoding the unfolding (déploiement) of a stratified space as an augmented semi-simplicial space Γ over the base Σ, indexed by finite ordinals with injective (cofinal) maps
ideas.modern_name: augmented semi-simplicial resolution / unzipping of stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (semi-simplicial resolutions for normal crossings, Hodge II/III, 1971–74); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (unzipping of conically smooth stratified spaces, 2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions 'déploiement' of stratified spaces only programmatically

ideas.what: Γ(d) = space of germs of codim-(d+1) strata, i.e. increasing (d+1)-tuples of codim-1 local branches, with face maps from deleting branches
ideas.modern_name: normalized multiple-intersection strata D^{[k]} / k-fold boundary ∂^k of a manifold with corners

ideas.what: 'Ordered' stratification: a continuously varying total order on local codim-1 branches at each point, given as a clopen subset of Γ_0×_ΣΓ_0 minus the diagonal with transitivity (next page). It replaces a global numbering of components.
ideas.modern_name: local (relative) ordering of boundary branches; orientation-type data making the boundary semi-simplicial rather than symmetric-simplicial
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; Deligne uses a global ordering, Jänich uses global faces

missed.claim: Grothendieck replaces a global ordering of components with a locally constant relative total order on local codimension-1 branches. This is exactly the minimal datum needed to turn the symmetric (𝔖_d-equivariant) structure of iterated boundary branches into a semi-simplicial space. The literature on normal crossings and corners usually assumes simple normal crossings with a global ordering, or works 𝔖_d-equivariantly; the intermediate 'locally ordered' notion is not standard.
missed.quote: et "ordonnée" (i.e. chacune des strates de codim 1 passant par un x ∈ Σ sont ordonnées, et cette relation d'ordre varie continûment avec x en un sens évident)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a clean intermediate hypothesis for semi-simplicial resolutions of non-simple normal crossings and corner structures, relevant to cubical/semi-simplicial hyperresolutions and to exit-path and unzipping constructions for stratified spaces.

missed.claim: The equivalence 'semi-simplicial relative space Γ satisfying b1–b3 ⇔ ordered locally cylindrical stratification of Σ', and the reconstruction of the unfolding spaces from Γ, are announced rather than proved here.
missed.quote: pour reconstituer les espaces de déploiement associés à la stratification, à l'aide des Γ(d), grâce à cette structure ordonnée
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early version of the reconstruction of stratified spaces from their unzipping or link data, as in Ayala–Francis–Tanaka. It could be compared with that work.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful set-up of known-type structure: semi-simplicial strata spaces for corner or normal-crossing stratifications. The relative continuous ordering and the déploiement viewpoint anticipate later unzipping constructions, but each ingredient is close to standard.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'Γ(X) = Σ^*(0)' should read 'Γ(∅) = …' (empty set, as on the previous page).

The base is written Σ^A(ω) / Σ^*(ω) in places (e.g. 'Σ^*(ω) = Σ' on line 6 and 'Σ = Σ^*(ω)' on the last line); '(0)' vs '(ω)' is ambiguous in the image. The superscript is likely the 'A' of the previous page rather than '*'.
'[-ordonnées-] ordonnées': the struck word appears to be 'sont', i.e. 'sont ordonnées'.
'en cas de germes de strates de codim 1 = ×' is uncertain; the image reads roughly '… en cas de germes de strates de codim 1 [struck] = Σ×', possibly identifying Γ(0) with germs of codim-1 strata.
